sentences.text: To find an estimated time of arrival, work out the running time and add it to your departure time.
Departing at eight fifteen, running twenty-two miles at sixteen knots takes sixty times twenty-two, divided by sixteen, about eighty-two and a half minutes, or one hour twenty-three minutes.
If your speed changes, recompute from your latest position.
And remember that current changes your speed over the ground, so a head current makes you late.
